outputs.explanation: Panel A is a domain map diagram and western blot images, not a data plot summarizing averaged measurements.

The bars represent single densitometry quantification values (FT depletion % and elution abundance) derived from the single blots shown in panel A; no error bars or stated replicate number indicate these are averages of multiple measurements, so no individual points are being masked.

The heatmap displays log2 average abundance (of 2 biological replicates) for 79 proteins across 4 antibodies. This large multi-protein matrix format cannot practically overlay individual replicate points per cell, and heatmaps are an accepted exception to the individual-points requirement.

Violin plots already depict the full distribution shape of the underlying protein-level enrichment values (not just a mean), which conveys spread/variability without requiring a literal point overlay given the large number of underlying proteins.
Caption explicitly states n = 4, mean ± SD, and the bar graphs show individual replicate data points (circles) plotted over each bar for Htt, F8a1, and Synj1 across the three antibodies.
Panel F is a sequence alignment schematic and predicted structural model image, not a quantitative plot of averaged data.
Each point in the scatterplots represents an individual co-isolated protein's log2 enrichment ratio; the plot inherently shows individual data rather than a summarized average.
The caption states the scatterplot shows correlation across 'all individual IP-MS experiments,' meaning each plotted point is an individual experiment, not an averaged value.
The PCA plot displays individual sample scores (one point per sample) rather than an averaged summary statistic.
As in panel I, the PCA plots show individual sample points stratified by antibody set, tissue, and polyQ length, rather than averaged group summaries.
